newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt maintains strong support - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt maintains strong support - poll.

text.p: The Australian government has entered 1997 with a solid lead over the Labor opposition party, according to a poll published on Thursday.
The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found the Liberal-National government's lead over the opposition increased to 13 percentage points in the December quarter from 11 points in the September quarter.
Primary vote support for the government was steady at 49 percent in the December quarter, while primary vote support for the opposition fell to 36 percent from 38 percent in the previous quarter.
Prime Minister John Howard enters the New Year with support from 53 percent of the voters surveyed, up one percent from the previous quarter's result.
But the poll found that support for Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has dropped to 23 percent from 25 percent.
Howard's satisfaction rating remained steady at 54 percent, while Beazley's fell to 42 percent from 46 percent.
The latest Newspoll is based on a re-analysis of surveys conducted during the period from October to December 1996, in which a total of 6,888 voters were surveyed by telephone.
